candidates.subject: pygmy slow loris
candidates.title: Hold everything
candidates.body: Something large moved below. I froze with one hand halfway to my mouth. It passed. My hand remained there a little longer, carrying on with the fear after the rest of me had finished.
candidates.proseStatus: Recover existing unillustrated episode6 verbatim. No author wording changes.
candidates.visibleScene: A pygmy slow loris lies partly suspended among leafy branches at night. Its face turns toward the camera; one curled hand is raised beside the face. Orange eye reflections are visibly caused by photographic illumination. No second animal or predator is visible.
candidates.fictionBoundary: The large passerby below, freezing response, earlier movement toward the mouth and delayed lowering of the hand are fictional. The source does not diagnose fear, document the preceding gesture, or establish a predator. The raised hand is beside the face rather than at the lips. A still can support the narrated suspended gesture without proving its before/after.
candidates.canon: Retain Sumi, Cat Tien lowland forest11.42,107.4, existing avatar, voice and all ten prior literal passages. Source Binh Thuan is provenance, not a move. Current southern species identification matches southern Vietnam; five current primary observation identifications agree. The image gives no reliable sex or precise age; no new sex/age claim or family event. Ordinary independent nocturnal episode at existing slot6.
candidates.payoff: Fear persists in a small bodily gesture after conscious relief. The actual curled raised hand supplies the specific visual anchor. This is an unchanged held premise, not an accepted event reused.
candidates.reviewFlag: Lead must judge the raised-hand/mouth-direction fit and image quality. Image is relatively dark with photographic eyeshine, but face, hand and supporting branches are distinct. Do not label it a documented defensive pose or infer venom use.
